ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced screening for all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against: EU consolidated financial sanctions list; UN Security Council consolidated list; French national freeze register (Registre national des gels); OFAC SDN and sectoral lists for USD transactions; PEP databases; FATF high-risk and grey-list jurisdictions. EDD required for PEPs, non-cooperative jurisdictions, and complex ownership. Suspicious transaction reports to TRACFIN under CMF Art. L.561-15. Banking AML risk tier Medium_Risk_Enhanced triggers source-of-funds and source-of-wealth review. IVD sector must also screen biological agents/dual-use items under EU dual-use Regulation 2021/821 and French export control rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); Infogreffe / RCS (https://www.infogreffe.fr); INPI data search (https://data.inpi.fr).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the compulsory language for incorporation filings and statuts. Corporate name may be in a foreign language if distinctive, non-misleading, and available; non-Latin scripts require official transliteration into Latin characters and certified French translation. Loi n° 94-665 du 4 août 1994 (Loi Toubon) applies to commercial documents. The name must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing RCS name, protected trademark, or reserved sensitive token.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory name reservation extension exists; name is allocated upon RCS registration. If greffe rejects: (1) obtain written refusal; (2) amend statuts with compliant alternative name; (3) refile via Guichet unique. For prior-right conflicts, negotiate consent/coexistence or file opposition/cancellation before Tribunal judiciaire/Tribunal de commerce. For refusal of RCS registration, appeal to Tribunal de commerce within 15 days of notification. For regulated tokens (ANSM, ACPR, AMF), obtain prior written authorization or remove token.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only as administrative registered office under Art. registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: ANSM/notified body initial and periodic audits 70–90% within first 24 months; unannounced tax/URSSAF/customs inspections 15–30% annually; EU IVDR notified body audits 100% prior to CE certification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, including Articles L. 210-1 et seq. (commercial companies), L. 227-1 to L. 227-20 (SAS), and R. 123-1 et seq. (commercial and companies register formalities). The SAS is governed principally by its articles of association, subject to mandatory statutory rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent local Registry of the Commercial Court (greffe du tribunal de commerce), with company-formation formalities submitted through the national Guichet unique managed by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic company-formation formalities (formalités de création) filed through the Guichet unique, including the declaration of creation and filing of the signed articles of association; the registry records the company in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A SAS has no statutory minimum share capital; €1 is legally possible, subject to commercial and financing needs. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid up at incorporation, with the balance payable within five years after registration. Cash contributions must be deposited before filing with an eligible bank, notary, or other legally authorized depositary; the funds are released upon presentation of evidence of registration. Contributions in kind are generally subject to valuation by a commissaire aux apports unless a statutory exemption applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscriptions for the shares set out in the executed subscription documents and acknowledges receipt of the amounts paid at incorporation, subject to the depositary’s certificate. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at the address stated in the articles of association, effective upon registration. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed President (Président) of the Company for the term and on the terms provided in the articles, and that [Name] is appointed [Director/Authorized Officer] with the authority specified therein. RESOLVED, that the President is authorized to complete registration formalities, provide supplementary documents, and make non-substantive corrections requested by the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Approve structure and execute SAS articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders and, where applicable, the appointed commissaire aux apports; filing is subsequently made through the INPI Guichet unique.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the corporate name, registered-office address, corporate purpose, share capital, share classes, governance rules, and President. Prepare and sign the articles of association and subscription documents. Obtain any required contribution-in-kind valuation report. No general notarization requirement applies to ordinary SAS articles; authenticate or notarize foreign-executed documents only where required for their evidentiary use or by the receiving institution.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association
Share-subscription and capital-contribution documents
Registered-office occupancy evidence and, if applicable, domiciliation agreement
Contribution-in-kind valuation report or documented statutory exemption
Identity and address evidence for founders and appointed officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies in the articles or supporting evidence, obtain missing signatures or valuation documents, and execute amended articles before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit cash capital and publish formation notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Eligible bank, notary, or other legally authorized capital depositary; authorized journal of legal notices (journal d’annonces légales) in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit at least 50% of subscribed cash capital and obtain the certificate of deposit. Publish the prescribed incorporation notice in an authorized journal for the registered-office department and retain the publication certificate. The notice must match the articles and formation particulars.
required_dossiers: Executed articles or draft articles accepted by the depositary
Subscriber identity and beneficial-owner information requested by the depositary
Evidence of cash subscriptions and funds transferred
Published legal notice and publication certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve depositary compliance queries by supplying source-of-funds, identity, or subscription evidence; correct and republish any materially inaccurate notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File creation formalities and beneficial-owner information
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique; competent Registry of the Commercial Court for RCS registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic creation filing, articles, capital-deposit certificate, legal-notice certificate, registered-office evidence, President’s appointment and acceptance, identity documents, non-conviction declaration and filiation information where required, and beneficial-owner declaration. Pay applicable registry and beneficial-owner filing charges. Respond through the portal to requests for correction or additional documents.
required_dossiers: Electronic company-creation declaration
Signed articles of association
Capital-deposit certificate
Legal-notice publication certificate
Registered-office evidence
President’s appointment, acceptance, identity evidence, and required declarations
Beneficial-owner declaration
Foreign corporate-founder documents, including registry extract and certified French translations where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address the registry’s stated deficiency through the Guichet unique within its deadline, upload corrected or missing documents, and pay any assessed supplemental fee. If registration is refused, pursue the applicable registry review or judicial remedy and refile after curing the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration corporate and tax formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique, French tax administration (Direction générale des Finances publiques), and relevant social-security authorities as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the registration evidence, including the company’s SIREN and RCS details, verify the registered particulars, release deposited capital, open or finalize the operating bank account, and establish accounting and tax records. Register for applicable VAT and payroll obligations before relevant activities begin. Maintain the statutory registers and file subsequent changes through the Guichet unique.
required_dossiers: RCS registration evidence and SIREN/SIRET details
Capital-deposit release documentation
Bank account and accounting records
VAT and employer-registration information, where applicable
Corporate statutory registers and governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inaccurate registry or tax records through the relevant filing channel; submit missing tax or social-security information and obtain professional advice on deadlines and penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: There is no general French industrial licensing board or universal manufacturing operating permit. The competent authority for an ICPE installation is generally the Prefect of the department, with technical processing by the regional DREAL or, in specified territories, the relevant environmental inspection service. Medical-device market-access oversight is exercised by the Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé (ANSM), alongside the applicable EU conformity-assessment and notified-body framework.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general operating-license title applies solely because the company manufactures IVD equipment. Depending on site activities and thresholds, the facility may require an ICPE declaration, registration, or environmental authorization under the French Environmental Code. In-vitro diagnostic devices placed on the EU market must comply with Regulation (EU) 2017/746 (IVDR), including applicable conformity assessment, CE marking, and registration and vigilance obligations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition; the competent environmental authority is determined under the French Environmental Code and may include the regional Mission régionale d’autorité environnementale (MRAe). DREAL provides relevant inspection and technical review.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Site-specific determination. Screen planned processes, chemicals, solvents, storage, combustion, wastewater, and waste against the ICPE nomenclature. Depending on the applicable rubric and thresholds, the facility may be outside ICPE scope, subject to declaration, registration, or environmental authorization; an environmental assessment is required only where prescribed by the applicable rules or screening decision.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No single threshold applies to all IVD manufacturing sites. Comply with the applicable ICPE prescriptions, water-law requirements, industrial sewer discharge authorization, and any prefectural order. Characterize and treat wastewater before discharge; control VOC emissions where solvent use and applicable ICPE thresholds require it; segregate, classify, store, and transfer hazardous and non-hazardous waste through authorized channels, with required tracking for regulated waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupancy, obtain any required building or planning approvals and comply with the applicable fire-safety rules for the building’s classification, including ERP requirements if the premises receive the public. Confirm structural capacity for equipment and storage through competent design review where relevant. Implement French Labour Code workplace risk prevention, occupational-health arrangements, fire precautions, emergency procedures, and required workplace inspections. Additional site-specific clearances may apply to classified installations, pressure equipment, chemical storage, or other regulated hazards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — French Public Finances Directorate; taxpayer portal impots.gouv.fr; customs authority Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) via pro.douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the SAS with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the CFE (Centre de Formalités des Entreprises) to obtain the 9-digit SIREN and 14-digit SIRET. Step 2: File French VAT (TVA) registration form Cerfa N°15417*03 with the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); for non-established foreign investors the application is handled by the Non-Resident Tax Department (Service de l'impôt des non-résidents) which issues the FR intra-Community VAT identification number. Step 3: Non-EU persons without an EU establishment must appoint a DGFiP-approved fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) for VAT compliance unless the non-Union OSS or EU VAT refund regime applies. Step 4: Apply to the DGDDI for an EORI number (pro.douane.gouv.fr) before first customs clearance. Step 5: Activate the SIE account on impots.gouv.fr and update the ERP master data with SIREN, SIRET, TVA intra-communautaire and EORI identifiers. Typical completion time for the French SAS is 4 to 6 weeks from formation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SAS is compulsorily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at the standard 25% rate (reduced 15% rate up to EUR 42,500 net taxable profit for SMEs with turnover ≤ EUR 10 million) on all profits subject to French domestic territoriality rules. No shareholder-level pass-through is available to an SAS under French domestic law and no US-style check-the-box regime exists. Territorial scope: France applies a worldwide taxation model for resident companies with foreign tax credit and branch loss mechanisms; certain activities implemented in overseas collectivities (COM) may benefit from territorial exemption regimes, but the mainland IVD manufacturing activity remains fully within the mainland French tax net.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid pass-through election. The material elections and mechanisms available to the SAS are: (i) intégration fiscale (group tax consolidation) under CGI Art. 223 A, allowing a 95%-owned parent SAS to consolidate French subsidiaries' results; (ii) the parent-subsidiary (mère-fille) participation exemption on qualifying dividend income (CGI Art. 145); (iii) the dividend and capital-gain holding-period tracking rules; (iv) ATAD 1/2 anti-hybrid recharacterization elections implemented under LOI 2019-1479 and CGI Art. 212 bis, which permit the recharacterization of hybrid instrument payments and entity mismatches to eliminate double non-taxation; (v) the EU OSS non-Union registration election for distance/electronic B2C supplies within the EU; and (vi) the customs authorized economic operator (AEO) certification elections for simplified export clearances. None of these mechanisms converts the SAS into a transparent entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), harmonized under EU Directive 2006/112/EC and codified at CGI Arts. 256 to 289, administered by the DGFiP.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for non-established foreign suppliers — any taxable supply (including B2B services, distance sales or domestic goods movements) that is deemed to take place in France triggers an immediate VAT registration duty without an economic threshold (CGI Art. 259-259 D; EU VAT Directive Art. 214). French-established micro-businesses may claim the franchise en base exemption (CGI Art. 293 B: EUR 85,000 for goods, EUR 37,500 for services) but this exemption is denied to foreign suppliers; the EU-wide EUR 10,000 distance-selling/Oss threshold applies only for intra-Community remote sales via the OSS regime. Because the entity is a French-resident SAS, it can never benefit from a foreign non-resident threshold and must register from the first taxable transaction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing the mandatory B2B e-invoicing and e-reporting reform (Réforme de la facturation électronique) with phased entry into force: from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and mid-caps (ETI), and from 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-enterprises. All French VAT-taxable persons must issue structured electronic invoices (Factur-X, UBL, CII in compliance with EU EN 16931) containing 10 mandatory invoice data fields, transmitted exclusively through a certified PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) or the national public portal (PPF). The PPF operates as the central tax clearance hub: invoice-level data and cross-border E-reporting transaction data are transmitted via authenticated APIs (HTTP represents JSON payloads) and receive transmission status identifiers (Statut PPF) for audit tracking. There is no current continuous-real-time digital stamping duty (unlike the Italian SDI bollatura), but tax-point clearance and reconciliation are effectively real-time once the invoice enters the PDP/PPF network; failure to issue compliant e-invoices triggers the DGFiP's automatic VAT declaration pre-validation and supports immediate reassessments. Cross-border supplies taxable in France performed by the French SAS will simultaneously be covered by E-reporting rather than e-invoicing mandates where the customer is not French-established.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating under CGI Art. 262-I applies at a 0% TVA rate where the French SAS exports goods (including IVD analyzers, microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay reagents) physically removed from France/EU customs territory to a destination outside the EU, provided the exporter proves (i) transfer of ownership to the non-EU buyer, (ii) physical movement of the goods out of the EU (exit must be evidenced within the regulatory export delay, generally up to 90 days), and (iii) appropriate customs export clearance via the DELTA-X system with a validated EXS (Export System) exit message. Export-related services — freight, handling, inspection, brokerage and international transport of exported goods — qualify for zero-rating under CGI Art. 262-II. Off-shore data, software and cloud services supplied by the IVD manufacturer to B2B customers outside the EU are outside the scope of French VAT under CGI Art. 259(1) (customer-location rule) and therefore do not need a zero-rating claim. The selling entity must record the export turnover in box 31 of its CA3 VAT return and retain the heteroclite export dossier for inspection.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DAU/ENS export customs declaration (déclaration en douane) cleared via the DELTA-X digital national customs system with valid EXS (Export System) exit summary confirmation

Commercial invoice and packing list issued by the French exporting SAS, describing the microfluidic cartridges/immunoassay analyzers with HS 3822.00 (IVD diagnostics) and ISIC 3250/NAICS 334516 product codes
Bill of Lading (ocean), multimodal bill, Air Waybill (IATA) or CMR road consignment note evidencing dispatch from EU customs territory and delivery to the non-EU consignee

Inward Foreign Remittance Certificate (FRC) and bank SWIFT MT103 confirmation evidencing EUR settlement of the export receivable from the non-resident buyer (export contract domiciliation under French exchange-control rules)
Incoterms delivery term sheets, carrier certificate of physical EU exit, and the French EXS manifest/port or airport exit stamps
Certificate of origin (EUR.1 / EORI-based origin declaration) where relevant for customs valuation or preferential regimes
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP and DGDDI jointly audit the fourfold export evidence pack (customs declaration, transport documentation, commercial invoice and FX inward remittance). Within the standard 3-year VAT reassessment window (extended to 10 years in cases of fraud, concealment or fictitious transactions under CGI Art. L.186 LPF), the authorities may retroactively deny the 0% rate and re-invoice French TVA at 20% on the exporter under the joint-and-several-liability rule of CGI Art. 283-4 whenever the physical export or the receipt of funds cannot be proven. The resulting default assessment carries: (i) a 40% penalty for serious lack of good faith or an 80% penalty for fraudulent behavior (CGI Arts. 1728 and 1731); (ii) monthly late-payment interest (intérêt de retard) of 0.20% per month accrued from each original VAT due date; (iii) under the French Customs Code, customs fines ranging between one and two times the value of the goods plus confiscation risk for fictitious export declarations; and (iv) criminal exposure for tax fraud (délit de fraude fiscale) pursued by the Parquet National Financier, including the disqualification and closure of the exporting SAS. In practice, exchange-control controls additionally require that export proceeds are repatriated to the French bank-account domiciliating the export contract within 180 days, failing which the outstanding amount is treated as an irregular financial transaction and may trigger withholding-reassessment and banking sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France and Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) acting under the European Central Bank's Single Supervisory Mechanism; foreign exchange policy administered by the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies full euro-zone capital account liberalization; the euro is fully convertible for current account and capital transactions. Profit remittances by a French SAS to non-resident shareholders are freely permitted, subject to the prior completion of statutory filing obligations, corporate income tax settlement, and the submission of Form 2561 or the report of payment of dividends to the tax administration. No prior exchange control authorization is required for dividend distribution or loan repayments, provided the transaction is routed through a licensed credit institution and the beneficial ownership documentation complies with French AML/KYC rules. For inbound capital injections by non-resident shareholders, the euro-denominated contribution requires no Bank of France foreign-exchange approval except in sectors subject to prior authorization under Decree No. 2019-1590 (foreign investment screening), which does not apply to IVD manufacturing absent technology-control triggers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no export proceeds surrender requirement. Exporters are entitled to retain all proceeds in foreign currency or euro accounts and are not compelled to convert receipts within any statutory timeline. However, proceeds must be declared in aggregate via the annual 'déclaration de change' under Article L. 152-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code where cumulative transactions exceed EUR 10,000 per calendar month; banking counterparties require standard underlying commercial documentation (invoice, bill of lading, customs declaration) under French anti-money laundering obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / EUR Trade Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / EUR Trade Settlement Account
Operational Account / EUR Trade Settlement Account / FX Forwards Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI cross-border viability is Limited. French-regulated electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Shine, and Treezor may provide operational euro accounts and payment initiation services, but are not viable for holding client escrow, trade-finance documentary credits, or large capital-injection settlement because they are not credit institutions, do not provide commercial loans or import/export letters of credit, and are subject to stricter activity limits under Article L. 521-3 of the Monetary and Financial Code. Offshore digital EMIs domiciled outside the EEA cannot legally provide payment services or hold accounts for a French SAS without a French or EU passporting licence, and would trigger French AML compliance rejection; their viability is rated Low for treasury operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the chairman (président) and at least one additional director (directeur général) or a duly authorized third-party with powers of attorney is mandatory for final sign-off at major French banks; remote opening is possible during pre-screening via video conference but physical in-branch verification is required for signature specimen and beneficial-ownership documentation. For a SAS, the legal representative must appear physically unless the bank grants a notarized procuration; in practice BNP Paribas and Société Générale require a physical meeting for the primary signatory. Remote onboarding for non-complex operational accounts may be accepted by certain fintech EMIs, but this does not satisfy the escrow and LC clearing requirements of this treasury stage.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry classification (ISIC 3250 / IVD medical device manufacturer) triggering enhanced due diligence under Article L. 561-5 of the French Monetary and Financial Code
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier A: French Health Products Safety Agency (ANSM) establishment registration; CE marking certificate under EU Regulation 2017/746; ISO 13485 quality-management certificate; three-year audited financial statements; business plan demonstrating genuine commercial activity and physical premises in France; list of final beneficial owners with French tax numbers; signed compliance attestation against financing of terrorism.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership chain involving non-resident shareholders of the SAS (Form 1231-SD non-cooperative jurisdiction flags)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier B: Corporate registry extracts (Kbis) for all entities in the ownership chain up to the ultimate natural person; identity documents and proof of address of each BO; organizational chart certified by the statutory auditor; shareholder register (registre des titres) for the SAS; declaration of non-resident BO tax identification numbers; notarized translations into French; explanation of source of wealth for each direct or indirect shareholder holding greater than 25%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital contribution funded from cross-border jurisdictions with medium AML risk or without clear source-of-funds trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier C: Bank statements from the remitting bank covering 12 months; signed source-of-funds declaration; transaction routing scenario detailing origin bank, intermediary SWIFT correspondents, and final French beneficiary; executed share-purchase/subscription agreement; proof of foreign direct investment declaration to Banque de France (Form 2260 for non-EU investors above threshold); evidence that funds originate from a licensed bank account in the name of the shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity expected due to point-of-care IVD trade settlements with distributors in non-EEA markets triggering Tracfin declarations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier D: Master distribution agreements; pro-forma invoices and underlying transport/insurance documentation; list of expected counterparties with KYC profiles; write-off and refund policy; internal transfer-pricing policy (TP documentation); customs broker mandates; monthly reconciliation procedure; commitment to file Suspicious Transaction Reports via the Tracfin portal where required under Article L. 561-15.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection routing compliant with French monetary regulation requires: (i) classification of payment purpose code as 'subscription of shares' or 'contribution to share capital' under the IMF BPM7 current-transfer classification, using SWIFT MT103 with Field 70 purpose 'CAPCONTRIB' or 'SUSB' and French Bank of France counterparty code 22019; (ii) funds remitted to the SAS's dedicated capital-escrow account (compte bloqué) at BNP Paribas or Société Générale; (iii) completion of the Banque de France financial reporting obligation for foreign direct investment through the 'Téléprocédure FDI' portal within 20 days after the transaction if the investor is non-EU or the transaction meets the EUR 15,000,000 threshold; (iv) verification of the declarant legal status and anti-money-laundering SOF (source of funds) documentation; (v) only after the full credit is verified and notarized by the bank, the notary's certificate of release (mainlevée de blocage) permits escrowed funds to be transferred to the operational account. All euro-denominated credits settle through RTGS TARGET2, with UETR (unique end-to-end transaction reference) mandatory for traceability.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for IVD analyzers and microfluidic cartridges are cleared via (i) SWIFT MT103 wire for routine supplier payments and distributor refunds in convertible currencies, carrying purpose codes 'Goods/trade' with copy of invoice and customs declaration in the payment file; (ii) commercial letters of credit (import/export LC) confirmed by BNP Paribas or Société Générale trade-finance desks, issued in euro or USD with SWIFT MT700, incorporating UCP 600 rules and Incoterms 2020; (iii) SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-denominated counterparties within France/EEA; (iv) B2B direct debit when recurring contract manufacturing is invoiced; disbursement above EUR 10,000 requires mention of the underlying commercial contract and customs reference to satisfy Tracfin vigilance and OECD 'carve-out' documentation; documentary trade settlements are preferred for Chinese or non-OECD raw-material suppliers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Euro/USD FX Forward (deliverable up to 24 month tenor) with licensed French credit institution, requiring confirmation under 2016 ISDA French Master Agreement or FBF Master Agreement
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for INR/CNY exposures where no deliverability exists, executed through Société Générale or BNP Paribas emerging-market desks, collateralized under CSA terms
Vanilla EUR/USD currency swap (cross-currency interest-rate swap) for long-term receivables or intercompany loan hedging, requiring separate ISDA CSA and internal-hedge authorization
FX option (plain vanilla call/put; premium in EUR) for purchase of USD in which the SAS hedges confirmed purchase orders of US-manufactured microfluidic consumables, licensed under MiFID II markups
Cumulative averaging forward for inventory-based monthly trade settlement when the bank offers an eligible rolling-hedge line

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Financial Statements (bilans and comptes de résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 4 months after fiscal year end (e.g., 30 April for calendar-year fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of 0.5% to 5% of unpaid tax per month of delay, potential company strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Statutory Audit Report (if mandatory)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same penalties as above plus possible nullity of accounts and director liability

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit if turnover exceeds 800,000 EUR, total assets exceed 400,000 EUR, or average employees exceed 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) or IFRS for qualifying large entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No mandatory annual confirmation required; UBO information must be updated in central register upon any shareholding transfer or control change

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 50-250 USD annually for registered office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,000-4,000 USD for small to medium SAS entities

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate in metropolitan France and overseas departments, subject to applicable territorial rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, generally subject to turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% ownership by individuals or qualifying entities. Qualifying research and development expenditure may benefit from the 30% French research tax credit on eligible expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold. Certain innovation, patent, and intellectual-property income may qualify for a 10% preferential rate, subject to statutory conditions, nexus requirements, and documentation. French tax losses are generally carried forward without time limitation, subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million; carried-back losses are generally limited to the preceding financial year and capped at EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional account using EFI or an accredited EDI provider. The return is accompanied by the 2058-A-SD and 2058-B-SD tax reconciliation schedules and, where applicable, the 2059 series, 2033 series, 2066-SD, 2069-RCI-SD, 2572-SD, and transfer-pricing schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; quarterly corporate income tax instalments are generally payable during the financial year, with a fourth instalment where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For financial years ending on dates other than 31 December, the electronic annual return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the return is generally due by the second business day following 1 May of the following year. The corporate income tax balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following the year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the balance is generally due by 15 May. Instalments are generally payable by 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, subject to statutory exceptions and adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, principal business activity, tax office, financial year dates, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not entered as the French taxpayer. The French SAS reports its own French tax identification and registered office and identifies foreign shareholders or related parties in the relevant schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or tax loss, corporate income tax due, credits, rebates, instalments, and balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French SAS's entity-level taxable result. Do not exclude profit attributable to foreign shareholders merely because ownership is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss adjusted for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, timing differences, depreciation limits, provisions, tax credits, and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include French-law adjustments for cross-border interest limitation, non-deductible distributions, withholding taxes, related-party charges, and expenses lacking business purpose or arm's-length support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year loss, carried-forward losses, carried-back loss where elected, and losses utilized against current taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the EUR 1 million plus 50% utilization ceiling for carried-forward losses and retain supporting computations. Foreign group losses are not directly deductible by the French SAS unless a specific French tax-consolidation rule applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treatment of disposals of fixed assets, securities, intellectual property, and other business assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify gains under French rules and separately analyze treaty allocation, especially for shares, intellectual property, real estate-rich entities, and permanent-establishment assets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2066-SD, tax credits and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible tax credits, including research tax credit and other credits, with supporting amounts and carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding tax credits require treaty or domestic-law entitlement, evidence of foreign tax paid, beneficial ownership analysis, and the applicable French limitation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary reporting of research tax credit and other refundable or non-refundable tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain technical project files, personnel and expenditure records, subcontractor certifications, and allocation evidence for IVD research and development activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2572-SD, corporate income tax payment statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax balance, instalments, credits, rebates, and amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made electronically from the French entity's tax account. Non-resident shareholder funding does not replace the SAS's payment obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of related-party transactions, nature and amounts of transactions, transfer-pricing method, and documentation status, where the statutory threshold or qualifying relationship applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border purchases, sales, royalties, management fees, financing, guarantees, cost-sharing, and other controlled transactions involving foreign related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certain expenses paid to related persons, including specified remuneration, commissions, royalties, and other charges requiring disclosure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report material related-party charges and retain agreements, benefit evidence, invoices, allocation keys, and proof of actual services.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: VAT return CA3 and European Sales List or equivalent EU reporting
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Output VAT, input VAT, intra-Community supplies and acquisitions, exports, imports, and reverse-charge transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French VAT rules to IVD equipment, cartridges, installation, software, spare parts, imports, and intra-Community transactions. Verify medical-device VAT classification separately from regulatory classification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted corporate income tax filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% for deliberate non-compliance and up to 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of law, plus late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month, subject to statutory limits and procedural rules. Incorrect tax returns may generate tax reassessment, interest, penalties, loss of credits, and transfer-pricing adjustments. Failure to submit required transfer-pricing documentation may trigger a specific penalty generally equal to the greater of EUR 50,000 or 0.5% of the amount of transactions for which documentation is absent, or 5% of the reassessed amount of transactions, subject to statutory limits.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate recipient, subject to domestic exemptions, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation, tax treaties, and anti-abuse rules. A qualifying EU or EEA parent may obtain exemption where statutory ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. French domestic withholding on dividends paid to non-resident individuals is generally 12.8%, subject to treaty and status rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility, test limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose anti-abuse provisions where relevant, and collect the applicable French treaty form or exemption certificate. The French payer generally withholds and remits tax through the appropriate French forms, including form 2777-SD where applicable. Treaty relief should be documented contemporaneously; where advance relief is unavailable, the recipient may seek a refund from the French tax administration. A certificate of residence does not by itself establish beneficial ownership, entitlement to treaty benefits, or EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties and similar payments to non-residents may generally be subject to 25% withholding under Article 182 B of the French Tax Code, subject to treaty reduction, EU or EEA exemptions, intellectual-property characterization, and anti-abuse rules. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax, except for specific statutory cases, including payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions or territories, certain profit-participating or disguised distribution arrangements, and other anti-abuse situations. Treaty rates vary by recipient residence and payment category and commonly range from 0% to 15% for royalties and 0% to 10% for interest, but the applicable treaty must be checked individually.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 for the principal full transfer-pricing documentation obligation where the French entity's turnover or gross assets meet the statutory threshold, where it belongs to a group meeting the threshold, or where another statutory control or group condition applies. A separate annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration generally applies at the lower EUR 150,000,000 threshold or where other statutory conditions are met. The Local File and Master File must be prepared and maintained in accordance with French requirements and OECD principles.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single, generally applicable economic-substance regulation equivalent to the UAE ESR regime. Substance is assessed through the French abuse-of-law doctrine, general anti-abuse rules, beneficial-owner analysis, permanent-establishment principles, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, anti-hybrid rules, treaty principal-purpose tests, and the requirement that expenses correspond to a real service and serve the company's business interest. The SAS should maintain French decision-making, qualified personnel, premises or operational capacity, technical control, inventory and risk management, IP functions, banking records, and contemporaneous evidence proportionate to its IVD manufacturing and distribution activities. A contract, invoice, or legal ownership record alone is insufficient where conduct and functions contradict the asserted arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of sales, fabrication of expenses, false VAT invoices, omission of taxable distributions, manipulation of inventory or customs values, or deliberate understatement of corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax recovery with interest and penalties; fraudulent tax evasion may result in imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with aggravated cases potentially reaching seven years and EUR 3,000,000, subject to the applicable facts and statutory provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil liability, and joint and several liability for tax debts where their fraudulent conduct or serious and repeated non-compliance made recovery impossible. Courts may impose professional prohibitions, asset seizure, and, where legally ordered, travel restrictions. The corporate veil is not automatically pierced solely because of control or ownership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT Carousel, Missing Trader, or False Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of fictitious suppliers, circular intra-Community transactions, artificial VAT refunds, false import documentation, or knowingly claiming input VAT without genuine supplies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, denial of input VAT, repayment of refunds, late-payment interest, penalties generally ranging from 40% to 80% depending on intent and conduct, and possible criminal prosecution for aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly organize or approve fraudulent VAT arrangements may face criminal fines, imprisonment, management prohibitions, and personal tax-debt liability under applicable French procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificial royalty, management-fee, financing, guarantee, procurement, or distribution arrangements that shift French profit without corresponding functions, assets, risks, or commercial benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment to arm's-length profit, withholding-tax consequences, interest, penalties for deliberate or fraudulent conduct, documentation penalties, and possible application of the French abuse-of-law or general anti-abuse rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed where they knowingly approve sham transactions, materially false documentation, or repeated non-compliance that prevents tax recovery. Ordinary disagreement over an arm's-length method does not by itself create personal criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Beneficial Ownership, or Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of a nominal holding or conduit company with no genuine functions to obtain treaty benefits, route dividends or royalties, conceal the ultimate owner, or defeat EU Parent-Subsidiary requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or domestic exemption, withholding-tax reassessment, abuse-of-law penalties, interest, and potential criminal consequences where concealment, falsification, or laundering is established. A shell company is not unlawful solely because it has limited operations; unlawful consequences depend on purpose, conduct, and applicable anti-abuse rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face civil recovery, criminal prosecution, asset confiscation, management bans, and personal tax liability where they knowingly participate in concealment or abusive arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify beneficial owners, unexplained third-party payments, sanctions-screening failures, suspicious wire transfers, cash structuring, or use of intermediaries inconsistent with the IVD business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory, administrative, and criminal sanctions may include fines, confiscation, account restrictions, business prohibitions, and imprisonment depending on the underlying conduct. French financial institutions may freeze or reject transactions and file suspicious-transaction reports with TRACFIN.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal criminal and civil liability for knowing participation, facilitation, or grossly deficient controls. Travel restrictions, asset freezing, and imprisonment may apply under the relevant criminal provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, Import Valuation, and Origin Misstatement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understatement of customs value, incorrect tariff classification of analyzers or microfluidic cartridges, false origin, evasion of import VAT, or use of inaccurate product descriptions or preferential-origin evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of customs duties and import VAT, customs penalties, seizure or forfeiture of goods, loss of simplified customs authorizations, and criminal sanctions for fraudulent customs declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible customs officers may be liable where they knowingly authorize fraudulent declarations or fail to maintain required controls. Personal exposure can include fines, asset seizure, professional disqualification, and imprisonment in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manufacture or placing on the market of IVD devices without required conformity assessment, CE documentation, technical files, post-market surveillance, vigilance reporting, traceability, or authorized economic-operator controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative orders, withdrawal or recall, suspension or prohibition of placing products on the market, destruction or seizure of products, civil damages, and criminal penalties under applicable EU and French medical-device laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal and civil exposure for knowing distribution of unsafe or non-compliant devices, falsified technical records, obstruction of regulators, or failure to act after a safety signal. Corporate limited liability does not protect deliberate misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: False accounts, concealed liabilities, unlawful distributions, misuse of corporate assets, preferential payments during insolvency, or continuation of a loss-making business through fraudulent representations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Nullity of distributions, restitution, damages, management bans, bankruptcy-related sanctions, criminal fines, and imprisonment for abuse of corporate assets, fraudulent accounting, or bankruptcy offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be ordered to contribute to all or part of an insufficient insolvency estate where management faults contributed to the shortfall. Criminal courts may impose imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and director disqualification.
